answers.answer: Dapper is a .NET micro-ORM: application code calls connection extension methods to execute SQL and map query results to objects, synchronously or asynchronously. The README identifies Stack Overflow as a production user. Repository tests also call it directly; this is a library, not an application with one universal main entrypoint.

Principal project components: Dapper is the core SQL execution/object-mapping library; SqlBuilder composes SQL; Rainbow adds CRUD helpers; EntityFramework supplies EF type handlers; ProviderTools supplies provider-independent ADO.NET utilities. StrongName builds a signed variant from core source. Tests and benchmarks are separate consumers. Within core, CommandDefinition carries operation settings and creates/configures commands.

Implementation is C# (repository LangVersion 13), with SQL supplied as strings. SDK-style .csproj files use .NET/MSBuild; Build.csproj uses Microsoft.Build.Traversal to aggregate library, test and benchmark projects. NuGet package IDs follow assembly names and package versions are centrally managed. Core targets net461, netstandard2.0, net8.0 and net10.0; companion projects have their own target sets. Core, SqlBuilder, Rainbow, EntityFramework and signed variants are separate boundaries; ProviderTools exists but is explicitly non-packable at this pin.
At Dapper.SqlMapper.Execute(this IDbConnection cnn, string sql, object? param = null, ...), Dapper/SqlMapper.cs:559. It constructs CommandDefinition and calls ExecuteImpl.
ExecuteImpl selects the single-command path; ExecuteCommand in Dapper/SqlMapper.cs:3004-3022 performs synchronous cmd.ExecuteNonQuery().

SqlBuilder directly depends on Dapper core. Its csproj declares ProjectReference to ../Dapper/Dapper.csproj, proving consumer → dependency direction. In source, Template.ResolveSql creates core DynamicParameters and resolves clauses into it. This is stronger evidence than a same-namespace/import heuristic.

Execute → CommandDefinition → ExecuteImpl. Null parameters make GetMultiExec return null and skip Identity/GetCacheInfo; ExecuteCommand receives a null parameter reader. SetupCommand creates the provider command, initializes it, assigns SQL, transaction/timeout/type, and skips parameter binding. ExecuteCommand opens an initially closed connection, calls ExecuteNonQuery, invokes OnCompleted (no parameter callback here), and returns its integer; finally it closes only an initially closed connection, clears parameters and disposes the command. Unresolved: concrete IDbConnection/IDbCommand implementations, provider initialization behavior, server execution, exceptions and actual affected-row count depend on runtime inputs/provider/database. This is source reasoning, not an executed trace.

Five direct project consumers are evidenced by explicit/inherited ProjectReference: Dapper.EntityFramework, Dapper.Rainbow, Dapper.SqlBuilder, tests/Dapper.Tests, and benchmarks/Dapper.Tests.Performance. Test and benchmark references come from their Directory.Build.props. Additionally, Build.csproj includes core through its Dapper*/*.csproj traversal glob. Dapper.StrongName is a separate source-sharing impact boundary: it compiles ../Dapper/**/*.cs rather than referencing Dapper.csproj. These are build/source dependencies, not proof every change alters runtime behavior.

README's non-result command example creates #t, inserts two parameterized values, drops the table, and asserts count 2. It calls connection.Execute(sql, new {a=1,b=2}), entering the string overload and the single-command path. The matching TestExecuteCommand is in MiscTests. This example has parameters; it is not evidence of executing the null-parameter scenario during this evaluation.

Z enters Execute's sql argument, then becomes CommandDefinition.CommandText. The constructor infers Text versus StoredProcedure when commandType is omitted. SetupCommand assigns CommandText to the provider command; ExecuteCommand executes it. With null parameters there is no parameter-reader rewrite. SQL interpretation/execution beyond that assignment belongs to the provider/database.
